sections.html:
Locals call it The Valley. Spokane Valley is the biggest suburb of Spokane, spread along the Spokane River between Spokane and Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, and it wraps around the separate city of Millwood on three sides. As of July 1, 2025 it had an estimated 108,405 residents, 5.2 percent above the 2020 base.

What is measuredSpokane Valley, 2020 to 2024
Typical value of an owned home$382,300
Typical monthly rent$1,353
Share of homes lived in by owners58.2%
Typical household income$74,042
Average commute20.8 minutes

Home prices are modest compared with the Seattle area, so the state's tiered excise tax takes a smaller share of a typical sale. The closing section below explains how.

Short commutes help here. A drive of 20.8 minutes on average is a plain, true selling point, and Interstate 90 access is the first thing many buyers ask about.

sections.h2: A city built from several communities
sections.html:
The city dates to March 31, 2003, when Dishman, Opportunity, Trentwood, Veradale, part of Greenacres and East Spokane joined together, with Yardley and Chester inside the boundaries too. That patchwork shows in the housing. Farm and orchard land became postwar subdivisions, and the streets bend, stop and restart, with many cul-de-sacs. Buyers still use the old community names, so mention the one your house belongs to when you describe it.

The incorporation came after years of debate about local control, and the city has stayed a patchwork of distinct areas since. If your house sits near a boundary with Spokane or Millwood, confirm the jurisdiction before you ask about permits, because the office to call changes with the answer.

Interstate 90 runs through the middle, and the city is reached by exits 285 through 293. Drive times are short for this region. Buyers most often name these routes:

  • Sprague Avenue, the main shopping street, which doubles as Interstate 90 Business.
  • Trent Avenue, State Route 290, heading northeast to the Idaho border.
  • Pines Road, where State Route 27 begins at its northern end.
  • Argonne, Mullan, Pines, Evergreen and Sullivan, the main north to south arterials.
  • Bus service from Spokane Transit Authority via the Pence-Cole Valley Transit Center, plus a few park-and-ride lots.

School districts overlap the city. Central Valley is largest, East Valley and West Valley follow, and part of the western edge belongs to Spokane Public Schools. Lines ignore city limits, so look up your address before naming a school in a listing.

Spokane Valley asks for a permit on new homes, duplexes, garages, decks, pools, spas and fences, and on any addition or interior alteration to a house. The interior point deserves attention if you did the work yourself. The Permit Center is inside City Hall at 10210 E. Sprague Avenue, phone 509-720-5240. Filings include site plans, construction plans and a copy of the sewer permit from Spokane County Utilities. The online portal accepts applications, with payment by check or by card plus a 2.5 percent convenience fee.

All businesses in the city need an annual state business license, and the city's general license costs $25 to start and $25 to renew. A home business needs a separate permit. Renting out the house? Call the Business Licensing Specialist at 509-720-5333 to find out whether a rental needs a license or registration.

Selling a single-family rental that has a tenant requires 90 days of written notice under RCW 59.18.650, and you must list within 30 days after the tenant moves out.

Payment runs through the Spokane County Treasurer, and the order of steps counts. The state's excise tax reaches nearly every sale. Bring the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit and the deed to the Treasurer first, and only then do they go to the Spokane County Auditor to be recorded. Cash or a check payable to the Spokane County Treasurer is accepted, but please do not mail cash. The Treasurer's number is 509-477-4713.

State tax starts at 1.1 percent on the portion of the price up to $525,000 and climbs above that. The median home value here, $382,300, falls under that first break. Beginning with sales on January 1, 2027 the break moves up to $551,000. The local rate is extra, and the Treasurer or your closing agent can quote it. Sellers usually bear the tax, and the state counts the notarized deed date as the sale date. A payment more than a month late accrues interest.

Because the Treasurer sees the paperwork before the Auditor does, a missing signature or an unfinished affidavit can hold up recording. Check every line before you drive downtown, and ask your closing agent to review the packet if one is handling the sale.

Each year Spokane County mails one statement with two tear-off coupons.

  • The first coupon is payable by April 30, the second by October 31.
  • Under $50, the whole amount comes due April 30.
  • If a deadline lands on a weekend or county holiday, payment is accepted the next business day.
  • Statement missing by March 31? Search the county's SCOUT system or phone the Treasurer.

Before signing a contract, ask the Treasurer what you currently owe. The closing agent then divides the year's property tax between you and the buyer, based on the closing date.

The buyer also needs the state seller disclosure statement, which is due five business days after the contract is accepted. The buyer then has three business days to rescind, unless the right was waived.

Do you have repairs you would rather not make? That alone can justify asking for a cash offer and holding it up against a listing. Listing opens the house to more buyers, at the cost of showings, repair requests and a wait for the buyer's loan. A cash buyer gets speed and certainty and pays a lower price for them.

The steps after an accepted offer are brief. Escrow opens, and the title company searches the record. Proceeds clear any loan, the deed is signed before a notary, and the affidavit and deed go to the Treasurer, then to the Auditor for recording. Funds arrive after recording. No appraisal or lender review is involved, so title work and your own calendar set the date.

At the first meeting, have the deed, a loan payoff statement, permit records and the newest tax statement on the table. Changed the interior without a permit? Visit the Permit Center beforehand so you know what an inspector might raise.

With a tenant in the house, give the buyer the lease terms before any offer is signed, and fold the notice period into your closing date. A buyer who knows the tenant situation up front is less likely to renegotiate later.

faqs.q: How many people live in Spokane Valley, WA?
faqs.a: Roughly 108,405 as of July 1, 2025, up from 102,976 at the 2020 census. Incorporation took place on March 31, 2003.

faqs.q: When are Spokane County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second. A bill under $50 is paid in full by April 30, and a weekend or county holiday moves the deadline to the next business day.

faqs.q: How do I pay the real estate excise tax on a Spokane Valley sale?
faqs.a: Bring the affidavit and the deed to the Spokane County Treasurer's office before the deed goes to the Auditor for recording. Cash or a check payable to the Spokane County Treasurer works, and cash should not be mailed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel before selling in Spokane Valley?
faqs.a: Yes. A residential permit covers an interior alteration to a home, duplex or accessory structure, along with additions, decks, pools, spas and fences. Call the Permit Center at 509-720-5240.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Spokane Valley house in?
faqs.a: That depends on your address. Central Valley, East Valley and West Valley cover most of the city, and part of the west is in Spokane Public Schools. Check a district boundary map before naming a school in a listing.
